explicit_bias_for.reason: Some validation reads must span old PostgreSQL systems during migration.

full_intake.free_form_notes: Several PostgreSQL databases and one vendor source are being consolidated. The PostgreSQL systems need publication/subscription migration with validation queries, while FDW is a transition tool for bounded reads. The migration playbook must cover primary keys, sequences, DDL, lag, and rollback.

recommendations.title: Logical Replication
triggers_for_next_stage: Move to a blue-green topology once replication lag, cutover checks, and write-freeze windows are defined.
why_not_yet: Logical replication still needs primary keys, DDL choreography, sequence handling, and rollback planning.
why_now: A PostgreSQL source plus zero-downtime migration need is a direct fit for publication/subscription cutover.

recommendations.title: Constraints
triggers_for_next_stage: Add append-only audit tables, actor identity propagation, and retention reviews once regulated workflows are mapped.
Escalate to exclusion constraints or RLS when overlap or tenant-isolation rules become explicit.
why_not_yet: If the audit scope is not yet named, start by identifying which tables and state changes require evidence.
If invariants are not yet known, start by naming the entity lifecycle and failure states before adding broad constraints.
why_now: audit_required posture depends on database-enforced state transitions, not only application logging.
Relational integrity gives audit reviewers durable evidence that invalid business states were rejected.
Relational core data needs database-enforced truth before optional architecture choices.
Constraints make bad states visible across every application writer.

recommendations.title: pg_stat_statements
triggers_for_next_stage: Use top total time and calls to justify the next index, schema, or topology recommendation.
why_not_yet: Ownership is still required: reset cadence, query text policy, and review rhythm should be explicit.
why_now: Workload decisions need normalized statement evidence before adding indexes, replicas, or extensions.
pg_stat_statements is low-risk and broadly available.

recommendations.title: Logical Replication Pair
triggers_for_next_stage: Move to blue-green once cutover gates and reverse-plan are written.
why_not_yet: DDL drift, sequences, replication lag, and fallback criteria must be owned.
why_now: A logical replication pair supports validation and controlled cutover for PostgreSQL migrations.

recommendations.title: postgres_fdw
triggers_for_next_stage: Require EXPLAIN VERBOSE pushdown checks and a materialization plan for hot remote reads.
why_not_yet: FDW should not become a hidden permanent hot path without pushdown verification and retirement planning.
why_now: The intake names remote PostgreSQL access and an FDW federation need.
postgres_fdw is the narrowest PostgreSQL-native bridge when remote paths are bounded.

recommendations.title: Composite Equality Then Range
triggers_for_next_stage: Adopt after pg_stat_statements identifies repeated tenant/status/time or account/time access paths.
why_not_yet: Column order must come from real predicates, not generic indexing instinct.
why_now: Hot OLTP and read-heavy filters often need equality columns before range or sort columns.

recommendations.title: Partial Indexes
triggers_for_next_stage: Adopt when pg_stat_statements or EXPLAIN shows repeated filters on status, tenant, active windows, or sparse flags.
why_not_yet: Partial indexes need proven predicates; without query traces they become brittle guesses.
why_now: Large OLTP tables often have small hot subsets that should not force full-table index maintenance.

recommendations.title: Partial Index for Skew
triggers_for_next_stage: Review index size and write amplification after one representative traffic window.
why_not_yet: Wait until the predicate is stable in application SQL and selectivity has been measured.
why_now: The index catalog has a matching pattern for selective predicates on skewed large tables.

recommendations.title: postgres_fdw Federation
triggers_for_next_stage: Document credentials, remote health monitoring, and fallback behavior.
Adopt once remote credentials, latency SLOs, and fallback behavior are documented.
why_not_yet: Avoid broad cross-database joins until latency and remote-owner behavior are understood.
Avoid broad permanent federation without pushdown checks and decommission criteria.
The rule matched, but weighted score is below the recommend-now threshold; confirm operational ownership, portability posture, and workload evidence first.
why_now: A federation topology makes ownership and remote failure modes explicit.
Migration-bridge workloads need explicit remote-source boundaries and owner-visible failure modes.

recommendations.title: PgBouncer
triggers_for_next_stage: Adopt once pool sizing, failover routing, and idle-session behavior are documented.
why_not_yet: Confirm application compatibility with transaction pooling, prepared statements, and session settings.
The rule matched, but weighted score is below the recommend-now threshold; confirm operational ownership, portability posture, and workload evidence first.
why_now: High peak connections on OLTP/read-heavy traffic should not map one application worker to one backend.

recommendations.title: Physical Replication
triggers_for_next_stage: Adopt when read routing, lag tolerance, and failover behavior are documented.
why_not_yet: A replica does not fix bad queries, missing indexes, or write bottlenecks on the primary.
why_now: Read-heavy systems can isolate reporting and expensive reads with replicas.

recommendations.title: Covering B-tree With INCLUDE
triggers_for_next_stage: Adopt when visibility map health and EXPLAIN show index-only scan potential.
why_not_yet: Covering indexes add write and storage cost, so projections must be stable and valuable.
why_now: Read-heavy stable projections may benefit from INCLUDE columns and index-only scans.

recommendations.title: PgBouncer in Front
triggers_for_next_stage: Test failover target changes and pool draining in maintenance runbooks.
Adopt after transaction duration, idle sessions, and prepared-statement behavior are measured.
why_not_yet: It cannot compensate for long transactions or inefficient queries.
Pool mode can break session-state assumptions and should be tested with the application.
The rule matched, but weighted score is below the recommend-now threshold; confirm operational ownership, portability posture, and workload evidence first.
why_now: Putting PgBouncer in front makes connection admission a topology concern.
Many concurrent sessions call for an explicit pooling layer in front of PostgreSQL.

recommendations.title: Primary With Read Replicas
triggers_for_next_stage: Adopt when read routing, lag tolerance, and consistency expectations are explicit.
why_not_yet: Replicas inherit bad query plans and introduce lag; they are not a first fix for missing indexes.
why_now: Reporting or read-heavy traffic may need isolation from primary write latency.

recommendations.title: Blue-green Upgrade via Logical Replication
triggers_for_next_stage: Adopt when dual-write avoidance, validation queries, and rollback owners are agreed.
why_not_yet: Do not promise near-zero downtime until lag monitoring and reverse-cutover criteria are written.
why_now: Blue-green cutover is plausible when logical replication is already part of migration planning.

recommendations.title: pgcrypto
triggers_for_next_stage: Adopt when URL-safe identifiers or database-side UUID defaults are explicit requirements.
why_not_yet: Do not treat cryptographic functions as a security architecture without review.
why_now: Database-generated UUID defaults are useful for public identifiers and distributed inserts.

recommendations.title: No Pooling With High Connections
triggers_for_next_stage: Add pool sizing, transaction duration, and session-state compatibility checks.
why_not_yet: Application pools may be enough if limits and transaction duration are already disciplined.
why_now: High peak connections without pooling evidence risks backend exhaustion and idle-session waste.

warnings.message: High peak connections without pooling evidence risks backend exhaustion and idle-session waste.
